title: Local Option Levy for Fire and Emergency Medical Services.
ballot_label: Local Option Levy for Fire and Emergency Medical Services. Question: Shall the District levy $1.06 per $1,000 assessed value for five-years commencing fiscal year 2027-28? This measure may cause property taxes to increase more than three percent.
summary: Stayton Fire District asks voters to replace its current levy with a five-year local option levy of $1.06 per $1,000 assessed value beginning fiscal 2027-28. The district says call volumes have increased and expenses surpass revenues; funding would maintain current staffing of 9 career Firefighter/EMTs, supported by volunteers, and help sustain response times. Estimated cost: $212 a year on a $200,000 assessed-value property.
yes_means: A yes vote authorizes Stayton Fire District to levy $1.06 per $1,000 assessed value for five years starting in fiscal 2027-28, replacing its current levy.
no_means: A no vote does not authorize the new five-year levy.
fiscal_impact: Estimated revenue: $1,459,638 (2027-28), $1,503,427 (2028-29), $1,548,530 (2029-30), $1,594,986 (2030-31), $1,609,290 (2031-32). About $212/year (about $18/month) for a property assessed at $200,000; estimate only. May cause property taxes to increase more than three percent.

collection_notes: yes_means/no_means: Oregon local ballot titles carry no official result-of-vote text, so these are neutral one-sentence descriptions written by the collector, grounded strictly in the official ballot question/summary. Arguments of kind 'explainer' on the YES side quote the rationale that the official ballot title/explanatory statement attributes to the sponsoring governing body; they are not filed pamphlet arguments. No comparable NO-side statement exists in the official text. Pamphlet access limit: WebFetch converts the Marion County voters' pamphlet PDF to only its first 118,524 characters (through p. 38, ending mid-sentence in the 24-528 explanatory statement); the Clackamas pamphlet (docs.clackamas.us/.../03f4f9db-...) is likewise cut off at p. C-33 in candidate statements. Pages 39-45 (remaining measures and any filed arguments) could not be read, so the existence of filed pamphlet arguments for 24-526, 24-528 (partly), 24-529, 24-530 and 24-531 is UNCONFIRMED; a verifier with full PDF access should check. Search budget: the shared WebSearch budget for this run was exhausted partway through step 3; the measure-number search was run for both sides, but the T3 allowed-domain search could not be run for either side. Equal effort was kept: the same searches ran for YES and NO. Marion's election page labels this 'Stayton Rural Fire Protection District'; the pamphlet and SEL 803 file name use 'Stayton Fire District'. A Statesman Journal article by Bill Poehler (syndicated on AOL, https://www.aol.com/articles/willamette-valley-voters-see-full-110126359.html, references the May 19, 2026 election) describes a Stayton Fire District five-year $1.06 levy replacing an 88-cent levy that runs through June 30, 2027; this suggests a similar levy was on the May 2026 ballot. Result not collected (no horse-race content). Inventory title matches the caption (including trailing period).
